title: Update objects in state with spread

slides.say: An object in state is read-only. You do not change it. You replace it with a new one.
This handler writes straight into the person object. React does not know anything changed, so the input looks stuck.
Instead, make a new object. Spread copies every old field, then you override just the one that changed, and pass it to the setter.

slides.text: Spread is shallow: it copies one level deep.
slides.say: One thing to remember: spread only copies one level deep. Nested objects need more work.
